landing.promise: Read what you'd read anyway. The words you meet come back — exactly when you'd have forgotten them.
landing.methodTitle: A word isn't learned once. It's met enough times.
landing.methodLede: Forgetting follows a curve: what isn't revisited is gone within days. Eaglish takes the words out of your own reading and returns them at the edge of that curve, where a single repetition is worth the most.

meet.p: Tap any word, anywhere in the app, and the translation fits the sentence it came from — not a dictionary's first guess.

save.p: It joins your collection with the sentence attached, so you remember where you met it and what it was doing there.

returns.p: Spaced repetition schedules the next meeting, and saved words stay marked in later texts — so the repeat never passes unnoticed.

landing.principlesTitle: Four decisions everything else follows from.

context.p: Words arrive inside sentences you wanted to understand. That's the difference between recognising a word and having it.

honest.p: Writing comes back with a real score and the specific fixes behind it. No inflated praise — you can't correct what nobody names.

short.p: Five focused minutes outperform an hour once a week. The streak protects the habit; it isn't there to guilt you into it.

ownLanguage.p: Navigate in Russian if it helps. The English you came for is never translated away.

landing.closeTitle: One text. Five minutes. Start today.

onboarding.testCtaHint: 10 adaptive questions, about five minutes. Every wrong answer is explained afterwards.

onboarding.stopTest: Stop and choose a level myself
onboarding.goalPerDayLede: One task is a text with its questions, a piece of writing, a lesson, or five review cards. Pick the amount you'd still do on a bad day — that's the number the streak protects.

pace.1: ≈2.5 hours a month. Modest, but unbroken: the same minutes spread across days are remembered better than one long sitting.
pace.3: ≈7.5 hours a month. The pace people keep for years — noticeably faster than five minutes, and it still fits into a day without planning.
pace.5: ≈15 hours a month. The fastest option here: Cambridge puts a CEFR level at 180–260 hours of practice, and this is the pace that covers one inside a year.

onboarding.changeLater: All of this can be changed later in your profile.
onboarding.promptTitle: Set up your plan — one minute
onboarding.promptBody: Four questions, or a five-minute level check. Without them the app has to guess your level.
onboarding.testResultNote: An estimate, not a verdict: twelve questions land on the neighbouring level about a third of the time. If it feels wrong, set the level yourself — it only changes which texts open first.
onboarding.planHorizon: For scale: Cambridge English estimates 180–260 hours of practice per CEFR level. Your pace is about {{hours}} hours a month — so Eaglish counts the tasks you finish instead of promising a date.

consent.title: What Eaglish keeps
consent.lede: Your theme, your language, your sign-in and your progress — stored so the app can work at all. No trackers, no advertising, nothing sold.

necessary.p: Sign-in session, theme, interface language and your learning progress. Switch these off and there is no app left to use.

analytics.p: Not connected today. If it ever is, it stays off until you turn it on here — and it will never be tied to your name or email.

consent.noThirdParty: All of it lives in your browser. Nothing on this list is shared with anyone, and none of it is a third-party cookie.

feedback.title: What went wrong?
feedback.lede: Anything at all: a bug, a confusing screen, a word you'd have written differently. The page you're on comes with the message, so no need to describe where you are.
feedback.placeholder: The review card wouldn't accept my answer…
feedback.sent: Got it — thank you. This is exactly what makes the app better.

insights.vocabularyExplain: An estimate: {{evidenced}} words you have proved directly — marked as known or held for weeks — on top of the {{assumed}} the placement level assumes. It moves as you prove more.
insights.comprehensionExplain: Share of the running words in our library you already know. Above 95% a text reads; below 90% it turns into decoding.
insights.retentionExplain: Across {{count}} scheduled reviews in the last month. This is the number that says whether the method works.
insights.retentionEmpty: No scheduled reviews yet — the first ones arrive a day after you save a word.
insights.forecastUnknown: Too few new words yet to project anything honest.
insights.collectedExplain: Every word you met in a text and kept. This is the number that grows on the days you show up.
insights.wholeVocabulary: Whole vocabulary, estimated: ≈{{total}} — the level baseline plus {{evidenced}} you have proved directly.
